correctness.rationale: For symmetric stochastic Φ, ||Φ||₂≤1 and I-rΦ² is positive definite. K=rΦ²+r(ζ-1)vvᵀ with v=Φe is positive semidefinite. Rank-one congruence makes ρ(K)<1 equivalent to r(ζ-1)vᵀ(I-rΦ²)^(-1)v<1; the trivial eigenmode contributes precisely 1/[M(1-r)], yielding the stated H_r threshold and equality/strict-reversal cases. Rayleigh on the all-ones vector gives ρ(K)≥r(M-1+ζ)/M; equality forces Φe uniform and that condition is sufficient by constant K-row sums. Exact reconstruction of five-by-five rational examples yields H=529543/11008272>1/24 versus 245/5956<1/24, with identical fifth columns and opposite determinant signs. Numerical checks of 120 further symmetric stochastic matrices corroborate only finite instances. The all-size conclusions rest on the rank-one and Rayleigh proof.
residual_risks: Only local disease-free invasion; requires 0<r<1, ζ>1, symmetric nonnegative stochastic mobility and equal resident populations.
No claim that rank-one linear algebra itself is novel.

value.rationale: The observable full hotspot column and its variance are shown insufficient for invasion: two exact five-neighborhood networks with identical hotspot mobility have opposite threshold outcomes as background travel changes. The all-size spectral budget supplies a precise invasion test, sharp uniform-column optimum and variance bounds. This directly advances motivated SIR mobility modelling beyond the special uniform-hub cases without claiming a new matrix theorem.
residual_risks: Threshold concerns local invasion only and not epidemic final size.

limitations: No directed, unequal-population, multiple-hotspot or global-endemic conclusion.
Earlier matrix rank-one test, uniform-hub quotient and source-era thresholds are prior art.
